forum.content_text:
Is there a detailed user manual available for the NUCLEO-U3C5ZI-Q?

[The product page](https://www.st.com/en/evaluation-tools/nucleo-u3c5zi-q.html) links to [a generic getting started document](https://www.st.com/resource/en/user_manual/um1727-getting-started-with-stm32-nucleo-board-software-development-tools-stmicroelectronics.pdf) and [a generic document on Nucleo 144 boards](http://a generic document on Nucleo 144 boards), but I can't see anything that lists the I/O or that documents the links.

scraped_replies.author: mƎALLEm

scraped_replies.html:
In my very humble opinion, documentation for Nucleo boards is bad, and this begins already at the product page in the main ST website. Descriptions are generic, fuzzy, send the user around many hoops to discover the characteristics of the board. User needs to quickly see what a specific board provides, including properties of the specific MCU and other components on the board: size of flash, RAM, etc. without downloading and browsing numerous PDFs.

Couldn't they get some spare AI agents to write decent product info pages?
scraped_replies.author: Pavel A.

scraped_replies.html:
For example, it would be really useful to have a single page showing all of the board that shows:

  1. Which transceivers are available on board (CAN, LIN, ...).
  2. Are any 8 or 16 bit wide ports available?
  3. Which peripherals have all their pins available on the various headers, which have reduced capability (half duplex, ...).
  4. ...
scraped_replies.author: CTapp.1

scraped_replies.html: Refer to the schematic is best to find which IO you want.
scraped_replies.author: EZHON.1

scraped_replies.html: I've tried to ask the Sidekick  about features of specific Nucleo board and it seems to know. It scanned the relevant PDFs and gives references. Would be cool if this thing were available on the whole site.
